[gap] = blank left by the copyist (margin signs given in the transcription). Uncertain readings carry over with "?". ## f. 14 = clear copy of f. 13 (Gualdo, 21 Jan 1447) Most illustrious Prince and excellent Lord, humble and devout recommendation. To carry out what Your Lordship charged me with at my departure, I inform you that today I arrived here, and tomorrow I shall set out towards Montefiascone [?], and there I shall wait until Wednesday morning to be informed by Your Lordship of your whereabouts, and where I am to come; not having anything else by Wednesday morning, I shall set out towards Monte Guiduzo, and from there I shall not leave until I am advised by Your Lordship of what I am to do; and I earnestly beg you to be pleased to send me a guide who is to guide me in your way. Further, I inform Your Lordship that Antonio da Trezzo is in company with me, so may it please you now to trust us [?], if you wish, that we come together or separately, because we shall all keep the order that will be given by Your Lordship, to whom I always humbly commend myself. Given at Gualdo, 21 January 1447. Of Your Excellent Lordship the humble servant P. de Pusterla To the illustrious Lord Francesco Sforza, etc. ## f. 27 = clear copy (Ferrara, 6 Feb 1447; cipher original not located) Illustrious and excellent Lord, humble and devout recommendation. This morning I arrived here, and at once I was with [gap], whom I found not without suspicion, for not having heard for days past from anywhere at what stage our affairs stand, etc. I used with him all the good words that were possible for me to remove his suspicion, without however revealing to him anything done, but I assured him of your good disposition, and urged him to be willing to come to the conclusion with [gap] soon; by means of which conclusion, whenever it should take place, I was certain Your Lordship would agree to everything that would please my lord, and what would be useful to the same [gap]; and so he suspected, indeed he was certain, that if His Lordship did not provide for the said [gap], the matter would come to no good end, and to the danger that Your Lordship might become vexed with the negotiation, etc. He answered me plenty of good words, which however are not of such effect that one can build great foundations on them; still he has charged me to carry some messages to the Duke on his behalf, showing himself well disposed. I do not know now what effect will follow, but I shall inform Your Lordship of everything. Marcolino Barbavara is going to His Holiness the Pope, and also to His Majesty the King, for the money business, etc., and because [?] what he is to do there about this will be laid on him by Your Lordship, and he not knowing how to write to you, having no cipher, I have given him the copy of mine, so that he can write, and so that no scandal may arise. Tomorrow I shall set out towards Milan, and I shall strive with all diligence to carry out what Your Lordship has charged me with, to whom I always commend myself. Given at Ferrara, 6 February 1447. Humble servant Pietro de Pusterla On the back: To the illustrious and excellent lord, lord Count Francesco Sforza Visconti, lord of Cremona etc., his most singular lord, etc. ## f. 33 = clear copy of f. 32 (Ferrara, 10 Feb 1447, per the margin note) Lord Count. Since I have been here I have heard nothing from Your Lordship, nor learned either at what stage things stand. I am here, and wherever I may be, I want Your Lordship to be certain that I am the usual Piero, and more a servant and more willing to do something that pleases you than for all the rest of the world; and so, if it seems to you that I should come here [there?] by one route rather than another, let me know, for I shall do everything that Your Lordship commands me. I beg you to be pleased to attend to your affairs while the time allows us. And may it please you sometimes to write me something, and to indicate to me what it seems to you I should do and say. ## f. 41r-v = clear copy of f. 42 (Milan, 14 Feb 1447; Mazzatinti 16 Feb) Illustrious Lord. I have arrived here, and by the [gap] our most illustrious Lord I was seen exceedingly willingly, and I reported to His Lordship in full what you charged me with, and so assured him of your true good disposition, at which he has remained so glad and content that I do not believe His Lordship ever knew what contentment was until now; and so I assure Your Lordship of it, that there is no man in the world better disposed, nor more inclined to live according to the will of another, than my said Lord towards Your Lordship, as I shall make you understand more fully on my arrival, which will be without any delay; and I would already have left, but it did not seem right to my said Lord that I should come without a good part of the money; and from Ferrara I shall inform Your Lordship of the day on which you are to send to Ferrara for the said money. Further, because the Lord wants me to make every attempt to induce the Duke of Ferrara to pay the expense of the Lord of Faenza, and about this he gives me the fullest commission, but because I am informed that the Duke of Ferrara, to pay the said expense, will want a promise of having something of what the enemies hold, and the Lord does not want any promise to be made to him of anything that the said enemies hold, except as far as shall seem good to Your Lordship, [gap] I beg you to be pleased to inform me straight away at Ferrara of your opinion about this, to gain more time, reminding Your Lordship well that the [?] said Duke of Ferrara has many lodgings [?] at Verona — [gap] and by offering him that, I believe he would make every great leap; but the Lord does not intend that anything be promised him, except as and when it pleases Your Lordship, to whom I always commend myself. Given at Milan, 14 February 1447. Of Your Excellent Lordship the humble servant Pietro de Pusterla To the illustrious Lord Francesco Sforza, etc. Marcolino Barbavara, Rome, 27 Feb 1447 (cipher f. 49; copy f. 48r-v) In Rome Barbavara finds Eugenius IV dead; the Camerlengo will wait for the new pope and is friendly; Capua and Fermo are tipped; a show of force in the Marche would loosen the cardinals' purses. Transcription: none of the cipher. The cipher leaf was not transcribed sign by sign: the late clear copy filed with it is a complete text (spot checks with the R1857 key agree). Decryption decipherments_18c.md # The filed clear copies (decipherments) of Barbavara's cipher letters, BnF italien 1584 Transcribed 28 Oct 2026 from the Gallica microfilm (ark btv1b100373864; canvas numbers in brackets) by Claude Opus 5.5. The copies are in one late, regular italic hand (eighteenth century to judge by the script; not dated), each on its own leaf filed before or around the cipher original. Spelling as written; line breaks not kept. `[gap]` = a blank the copyist left; `[?]` = my uncertain reading; `{...}` = my note. ## f. 39 = decipherment of f. 40 (Rimini, 13 Feb 1447) [canvas 36] Se lo cavalario {written above a word struck through} non ha servati quelli modi haveria voluto V.S. — {dash in the copy}, é proceduto, perché essendole quelli del [gap], non li pariva bisognasse venire [blot] cum altro reguardo. Adesso lo ho ammonito quanto bisogna, et capitarà a casa de Cecho vostro canzelero quanto scriveti. Mando per lui lo salvoconducto richesto per quelli dui vostri, et mercordì proximo andarò a [Atachio?] per la via de San Joanne in Marignano secondo el comandamento vostro, et servarò tutti quelli modi che loro me darano per retrovarme cum V.S. Cum lo Segnore Sigismondo ho servato lo modo del quale me avisa la Excellentia vostra, a la quale me recomando. Arimini tertiodecimo Februarij. Servitor vestre Dominationis Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 48r-v = decipherment of f. 49 (Rome, 27 Feb 1447) [canvases 45 right, 46 left] Illustris et excelse domine honorandissime. Essendo zonto qua ho trovato el Papa essere passato de questa vita come haveriti inteso, et ha pur voluto fare come diceva la S.V., cioè morire per fare male non solamente vivendo, ma etiandio morendo. Sono stato cum lo Camerlengo — {dash in the copy} lo quale intesa la casone de la mia venuta dice [blot] effecto essere necessario expectare la elecion d'un altro Papa, et per tractare la cossa cum la soa Sanctità, et che fra questo mezo posso andare da la Majestà del Re per strenzere la cossa cum si, et cussì farò, et de quello seguirà la S.V. ne serà avisata. Ha havuto el dicto Camerlengo molto grato et accepto quanto li ho dicto per vostra parte, et per le parole ha usato cum mi me pare essere molto volunteroso de havere et servare bona amicitia cum la S.V., et me ha commesso ve scriva che siati de bona voglia, perché qualuncha sia electo al papato voluntera farà de le cosse ve piaceranno. Dice etiandio ch'el serà amico el Segnore vostro padre, o almancho non li serà inimico, ma più crede che li serà amico e favorevele, et dio voglia che cussì sia. Se ha opinione che la elecione debia tocare o a Monsignore de Capua, o a Monsignore de Fermo, pur poteria essere che tocaria ad altri, perché me pare che sempre tochi a quello del quale comunamente non s'è facto pensiero. Se la Excellentia vostra facesse qualche vista et demostracione de volerse fare inance ne la Marcha, o altrove, siché qua ne venisse novelle, credo seria assay utile a rescaldare li animi de questi preti, et a farli più caldi al contribuire a la spesa vostra; et questo dico perché se [ha?] facto fondamento quasi certo che la S.V. ad ogni modo andarà a li favori et subsidii del {struck: del} a el prefato Signore vostro padre. La quale opinione però me sono sforzato de cavarli de la testa, et dicto che tale fondamento è vano, et che bene siati ben disposito bisogna che questa bona disposizione sia aiutata altramente che cum parole, cioè cum dinari. Ma per levargela ancora [gap?] {line ends with a flourish} Ex Roma vigesimo septimo Februarij. Vestre Excelencie Servulus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 55r-v, 57r = decipherment of f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) [canvases 53 right, 54 left, 55 right] Illustris ac excellens domine honorandissime. Sono stato da la Majestà del Re, et cum quelle rasone me sono acadute a la mente lo confortata et pregata a nome del mio Signore a prendere tanto majore cura et caricho de contribuire a la spesa vostra, quanto el bisogno è majore per la morte del Papa, dal quale non è più da expectare subventione alcuna. In effecto la soa Serenità è restata contenta non solamente de pagare quelo devia pagare el Papa, ma etiandio de contribuire de majore quantità non era stato rasonato da prima, cioè de ducati novantaquatro milia d'oro et in oro ogni anno et per dui anni come ha scripto el prefato Signore che'l restava contento de dui anni, et vole pagare li dicti dinari in questo modo, cioè vintimilia ducati nel mese presente, et altri xx m nel mese d'Aprile sequente al più tardi, et lo resto per la mità al fine de li sei mesi dal dì de la ferma vostra, et l'altra mità al fine del ano, et questo per lo primo anno: ma per respecto al secondo anno resta contento per tuto Martio del dicto anno de pagare quarantamilia ducati, et li altri LIIII m de sei mesi in sei mesi come è dicto de sopra, et cussì ha promesso la soa Serenità per capituli firmati et conclusi cum si et sigilati del suo sigillo, et ancora sotoscriti de soa propria mano: et debbe fare exbursare li dicti dinari a li tempi a qualuncha messo del prefato Signore, o vostro havendo expediente mandato a ciò. Per parte del Signore li è promesso, che non fareti contrasini contra li suoi, immo che bisognando mandarà el prefato Signore in suo aiuto, o tanti de li vostri, o de le altre gente ducale quante monta la spesa quale el fa per la conducta vostra, et ancora li è promesso, che quello pagherà el Papa serà electo debia pervenire in la soa Majestà. Per tanto de tuto aviso la Excelentia vostra acciò sapia quello è facto, et a bona fede doe cosse recordo. La prima che, o la Excelentia del Signore, o vui provediati de uno, quale habia mandato expediente a recevere el dinaro, et a confessare de haverlo recevuto, et ancora possa solicitarlo presso la Majestà del Re, perché sapeti bene, che dove va el dinaro non se po usare troppo diligentia. La secunda, che'l me pare necessario chiarire la prefata Majestà quanto più presto se po, come la conclusione è facta cum lui, aciò non se possa excusare, che per non essere chiarita non habia facta provisione al dinaro. Io li ho ben dato bona speranza de la conclusione secundo quello me dixe V.S., ma questo non credo che basti, et da mi non procederia a farli altra chiarezza, non havendo altro, o dal Signore, o da V.S., la quale me poterà scrivere la intentione soa circha de ciò {ciò written above a blotted word}, et io senza expectare altro la exequirò. Aviso ancora la excelentia vostra, che la Majestà del Re intende che in la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati, quali debe pagare, se includano li xx m del [gap; the copyist drew the cipher sign ꝺ+÷ in the margin]: Ma lui prende el caricho de fare che li pagli, e presto. Et per questo subito mandarà uno de li suoy, et pagandoli non se computavano in la quantità de li dicti xl m ducati se debeno pagare in Marcio et Aprile, ma in li altri se debeno pagare de sei mesi in sei mesi, et quando etiandio el [gap; ꝺ+÷ in the margin] non ne pagasse alcuna parte, resta però obligata la Majestà del Re a pagare la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati ogni anno. Se havesse possuto fare meglio, al che me sono sforzato quanto m'è stato possibile, lo haveria facto voluntera, ma non possendo ho acceptato quello ho possuto obtenere. Quanto a la elecione del Papa ve ho scripto per altre quello haveva inteso, adesso non me occorre altro, excepto che tutto se farà per haverne uno che sia amico, et non volendo esserlo se haverano de li modi da farlo pentire. Me recomando a V.S. et etiandio a la illustre Madona Bianca. Ex Roma tertio Marcij. Servitor devotus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 61r = decipherment of f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) [canvas 58 right] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Respondendo brevemente a quello me scrive la Excellentia Vostra per letre date a vintasete dal passato, dico che'l correro ducale, quale havite fato accompagnare, non me ha portato altra letra cha la vostra; sento bene che ne ha portate de le altre al Vescovo de Novara et a Misere Petro de Monferrato, et anchora a Simone Henrigono famiglo dal Signore vostro Padre, quale za molti meyse per la Signoria {"per la Signoria" underlined, "-ria" above} soa fa dimora in questo lito. Dico etiamdio che per tre meie {blot in the margin} ho avisato V.S. ____ de la morte dal Papa ____ {two underlined blanks} et de quanto me acadeva circha de ciò, ni da poy s'è innovato altro, excepto che li Cardinali questa sira sono intrati in conclave, et sperasse che assay tosto elezerano un altro Papa, et molto sono le opinione diverse a chi debia tocare la ellectione: Dio vegla che bona sia. Simelmente ho avisato per altre letre de la conclusione facta cum la Majestà dal Re. Et cussì le prime, como le segonde letre ho mandate a le mane de la Magnifica Madona Aura secondo me disse V.S., et per messi certi, e debeno le dicte letre esser zonte a salvamento. Da mo innance drizarò simile letre a Misser Angelo in Urbino como scriviti. Et continuamente avisarò V.S. de le cosse come passarano. Adesso ve mando alligate a le presenti certe letre de la Majestà dal Re, per le quale intenderite la bona dispositione soa, avisando V.S. che la intesso molto voluntera quello li ho dicto per vostra parte, et maxime ha gustato quello dicesti de havere alienato l'animo da le cosse del reame, et demonstrato una bona voluntà de volerve havere per tuto suo. Me recommando a la S.V. Ex Roma die quarto Martii 1447. per V.S. servitorem devotum Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 68 = decipherment of f. 69 (Rome, 6 Mar 1447) [canvas 65, upper leaf] Illustris ac excellens domine honorandissime. In questa hora decima septima, o circha, è publicato Papa Monsignore da Cologna {so in the copy: Tommaso Parentucelli, elected as Nicholas V on 6 March 1447, was cardinal-bishop of Bologna; the cipher was not checked at this word}. Credo firmamente che serà amico, e presto me sforzarò de vederne la experientia circa le cosse me sono comesse. Et de quello seguirà V.S. ne serà avisata, la quale me po avisare, se gli pare che sia da servare per mi più uno modo che un altro. Me ricommando a la Excelencia vostra. Ex Roma sexto Marcij 1447. Per Servitorem V.V. Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francischo Sfortie etc. ## f. 74r-v = decipherment of f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) [canvases 71 right, 72 left] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Da poi ve scripsi la ellectione del novo Papa sono stato quello dì de la ellectione per non perdere tempo a li pedi de la soa Beatitudine, et da poy alchune parole generale dicte reallegrandome a nome del Duca de la ellectione soa toccai etiandio el facto del dinaro per V.S.; in effecto me pare che la Sanctità soa insieme cum li Cardinali habia presso deliberatione de procurare pace in Italia, et de mandare per questa caxone el Camerlengo et lo Vicecanciellero insieme da la Majestà del Re, quale sono partiti questo dì, ma no li reusirano li pensieri, perché lo Re, dal quale sono stato per questa casone un'altra volta, delibera de darli molto bene ad intendere, et specialmente al Camerlengo, perché l'altro è Veneciano, che queste parole de pace non gli piaceno, excepto se non fano prima la provisione del dinaro per V.S., et de le gente per mandare insieme cum la soa Majestà, a ciò che cum questa via sia proveduto a la securezza del stato del prefato Duca, et li inimici temendo le provisione se reducano a meglore condictione de pace, o non volendola per amore se gli possa redure cum la forcia. Delibera etiandio la soa Majestà, se questo parlare non moverà el Papa et li Cardinali a fare altra deliberatione meglore et più grata de aprirli come essa Majestà intende tore in si el carrego de pagare la spesa vostra, et dire che siano certi ge la farà pagare tuta a loro, et se anchora questo non aiutarà, mostra de volere usare altro che parole, cioè venire a li facti dicendo, che li preti sono homini da bastonate, non da pregare. Non so quello seguirà, pur non sono anchora sanza speranza, che'l Papa et li Cardinali intendando el malcontentamento del Re se debiano movere a piglare meglore deliberatione; de quello seguirà V.S. ne sarà avisata; et forse como per altre ho scripto non serà altro, che bene che V.S. facia de le demonstratione per timorezare anchora più la brigata et redurla a quello desideramo. Ho recordato anchora a la Majestà del Re el facto de li dinari per V.S., et me ha resposto che sanza fallo li meterà tale ordine non vi mancharano a li termini, et simelmente ha dicto che in questa septimana aviarà el suo, quale el manda dal Signore [gap; the copyist drew ꝺ+÷ in the margin] per quelli vinti millia ducati. Me ricommando a la Excellentia Vostra, et maraviglo che da si non habia mai havuto ni letra ni risposta. Ex Roma die octavo Marcij 1447. per Servitorem devotum Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. Translation decipherments_18c_en.md # English translation of the clear copies of Barbavara's cipher letters (BnF italien 1584) Translated 28 Oct 2026 by Claude Opus 5.5 from `decipherments_18c.md`. [gap] = a blank left by the copyist; [?] = uncertain. ## f. 39 = f. 40 (Rimini, 13 Feb 1447) If the courier has not kept the ways Your Lordship would have wished, it came about because, those of the [gap] being his, it did not seem to him that he needed to come with any other caution. Now I have warned him as much as is needed, and he will call at the house of Cecco, your chancellor, as you write. I send by him the safe-conduct requested for those two men of yours, and next Wednesday I shall go to [Atachio?] by way of San Giovanni in Marignano, according to your command, and I shall keep all the ways they give me for finding myself with Your Lordship. With Lord Sigismondo I have kept the manner Your Excellency advises me of; to whom I commend myself. Rimini, 13 February. Your Lordship's servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 48r-v = f. 49 (Rome, 27 Feb 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Having arrived here I found the Pope had passed from this life, as you will have heard, and he has indeed wished to do as Your Lordship used to say: to die so as to do harm not only living but also dying. I have been with the Camerlengo, who, having heard the reason for my coming, says that in effect it is necessary to wait for the election of another Pope and to treat the matter with His Holiness, and that meanwhile I can go to His Majesty the King to tighten the matter with him; and so I shall do, and Your Lordship will be told what follows. The said Camerlengo received very gratefully all I told him on your behalf, and from the words he used with me he seems to me very willing to have and keep good friendship with Your Lordship. He charged me to write to you to be of good heart, because whoever is elected to the papacy will gladly do things that please you. He says too that he will be a friend of the lord your father, or at least not his enemy, but rather believes he will be his friend and favourable, and God grant it be so. It is thought that the election must fall either to Monsignor of Capua or to Monsignor of Fermo; yet it could be that it falls to others, because it seems to me it always falls to the one no one has commonly thought of. If Your Excellency made some show and demonstration of wanting to advance into the Marche or elsewhere, so that news of it came here, I believe it would be very useful to warm the minds of these priests and make them hotter to contribute to your expenses; and I say this because they have built an almost certain foundation that Your Lordship will in any case go to the favour and help of the said lord your father. That opinion, however, I have striven to get out of their heads, and said that such a foundation is vain, and that, though you are well disposed, this good disposition must be helped otherwise than with words, that is with money. But to take it from them still [gap?]. Rome, 27 February. Your Excellency's little servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## ff. 55r-v, 57r = f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. I have been to His Majesty the King, and with such reasons as came to mind I urged and begged him, in the name of my lord, to take all the greater care and burden of contributing to your expenses as the need is greater through the death of the Pope, from whom no subsidy is to be expected any more. In effect His Serenity has been content not only to pay what the Pope was to pay, but also to contribute a greater sum than had first been discussed, namely ninety-four thousand ducats of gold, in gold, every year and for two years, as the said lord wrote that he was content with two years. He will pay the said money in this way: twenty thousand ducats this month, and another twenty thousand in the coming month of April at the latest, and the rest half at the end of six months from the day of your engagement and the other half at the end of the year, and this for the first year; but for the second year he is content to pay forty thousand ducats by the whole of March of that year, and the other 54 thousand from six months to six months as said above. And so His Serenity has promised, by articles signed and concluded with him, sealed with his seal and also signed in his own hand; and he is to have the said money paid out at the due times to whatever messenger of the said lord, or of yours, holds a sufficient mandate for it. On the lord's part he has been promised that you will make no attacks on his men; rather, if need be, the said lord will send to his aid either as many of your men, or of the other ducal troops, as amounts to the expense he bears for your condotta; and he has also been promised that what the Pope pays, once he is elected, shall come to His Majesty. Of all this I inform Your Excellency so that you know what has been done, and in good faith I recall two things. The first: that either His Excellency the lord or you provide someone with a sufficient mandate to receive the money and to acknowledge receiving it, and also to press for it with His Majesty the King, because you know well that where money is concerned one cannot use too much diligence. The second: it seems to me necessary to make clear to His Majesty as soon as possible that the conclusion has been made with him, so that he cannot excuse himself that, not having been made certain, he has not provided the money. I have indeed given him good hope of the conclusion according to what Your Lordship told me, but I do not think that is enough, and from my side I would not go on to give him any other assurance, having nothing else either from the lord or from Your Lordship, who may write to me your intention about this, and I shall carry it out without waiting for anything else. I inform Your Excellency also that His Majesty the King understands that in the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats which he is to pay are included the 20 thousand of the [gap: the lord of Ferrara?]; but he takes on himself the burden of making him pay them, and soon. For this he will at once send one of his men, and when they are paid they will not be counted in the said 40 thousand ducats to be paid in March and April, but in the others to be paid from six months to six months; and even if the [gap: lord of Ferrara?] paid no part of them, His Majesty the King remains bound to pay the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats every year. Had I been able to do better, which I strove for as far as was possible, I would gladly have done it; but not being able, I accepted what I could obtain. As for the election of the Pope, I wrote to you in other letters what I had heard; now I have nothing else to add, except that everything will be done to have one who is a friend, and if he will not be, they will have ways to make him repent. I commend myself to Your Lordship and also to the illustrious Madonna Bianca. Rome, 3 March. Devoted servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 61r = f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Replying briefly to what Your Excellency writes to me in letters of the twenty-seventh of last month, I say that the ducal courier whom you had escorted brought me no letter but yours; I hear indeed that he brought others to the Bishop of Novara and to Messer Pietro of Monferrato, and also to Simone Arrigoni, servant of the lord your father, who has stayed in this place many months for His Lordship. I say also that by three letters of mine I have informed Your Lordship of the death of the Pope and of what happened to me about it; nor has anything new happened since, except that the cardinals entered the conclave this evening, and it is hoped they will very soon elect another Pope, and opinions are very divided as to whom the election should fall to: God grant it be a good one. Likewise I informed you by other letters of the conclusion made with His Majesty the King. Both the first and the second letters I sent into the hands of the Magnificent Madonna Aura, as Your Lordship told me, and by sure messengers, and the said letters should have arrived safely. From now on I shall direct such letters to Messer Angelo in Urbino, as you write. And I shall continually inform Your Lordship of things as they happen. Now I send you, enclosed with these, certain letters of His Majesty the King, by which you will understand his good disposition; informing Your Lordship that he heard very gladly what I told him on your behalf, and above all he relished what you said of having turned your mind from the affairs of the Kingdom, and showed a good will to have you wholly his. I commend myself to Your Lordship. Rome, 4 March 1447, by Your Lordship's devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 68 = f. 69 (Rome, 6 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. At this seventeenth hour or about, Monsignor of "Cologna" [so the copy; Tommaso Parentucelli, cardinal of Bologna] has been proclaimed Pope. I firmly believe he will be a friend, and I shall soon strive to see proof of it in the matters entrusted to me. Of what follows Your Lordship will be informed; and you may tell me whether it seems to you that one way rather than another should be kept by me. I commend myself to Your Excellency. Rome, 6 March 1447, by Your Lordship's servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 74r-v = f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Since I wrote to you of the election of the new Pope, I was, on the very day of the election, so as to lose no time, at the feet of His Holiness, and after some general words rejoicing in the name of the Duke at his election I touched also on the matter of money for Your Lordship. In effect it seems to me that His Holiness together with the cardinals has resolved to procure peace in Italy, and for this reason to send the Camerlengo and the Vice-Chancellor together to His Majesty the King; they left today, but their plans will not succeed, because the King, whom I have seen again for this reason, means to make them understand very well, and especially the Camerlengo (because the other is a Venetian), that these words of peace do not please him unless they first make provision of money for Your Lordship, and of troops to send together with His Majesty, so that by this way the security of the state of the said Duke is provided for, and the enemies, fearing the provisions, are brought to better terms of peace, or, not wanting it out of love, can be brought to it by force. His Majesty resolves also, if this speech does not move the Pope and the cardinals to some better and more agreeable resolution, to declare to them that His Majesty means to take on himself the burden of paying your expenses, and to tell them to be sure he will make them pay it all, and if even this does not help, he shows he will use other than words, that is, come to deeds, saying that priests are men to be beaten, not begged. I do not know what will follow; still I am not yet without hope that the Pope and the cardinals, understanding the King's discontent, may be moved to take a better resolution; of what follows Your Lordship will be informed. And perhaps, as I have written elsewhere, nothing else will do but that Your Lordship make some demonstrations, to frighten the company still more and bring it to what we desire. I reminded His Majesty the King again of the matter of the money for Your Lordship, and he answered that without fail he will give such orders that it will not fail you at the terms, and likewise he said that this week he will send his man, whom he is sending to the lord [gap: of Ferrara?] for those twenty thousand ducats. I commend myself to Your Excellency, and I marvel that I have never had from you either letter or answer. Rome, 8 March 1447, by your devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. Marcolino Barbavara, Rome, 3 Mar 1447 (cipher f. 56; copy ff. 55r-v, 57r) King Alfonso agrees to pay Sforza's condotta, 94,000 ducats a year for two years, on a schedule that includes 20,000 owed by the Duca di Ferrara, which the King will make him pay. Servitor vestre Dominationis Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 48r-v = decipherment of f. 49 (Rome, 27 Feb 1447) [canvases 45 right, 46 left] Illustris et excelse domine honorandissime. Essendo zonto qua ho trovato el Papa essere passato de questa vita come haveriti inteso, et ha pur voluto fare come diceva la S.V., cioè morire per fare male non solamente vivendo, ma etiandio morendo. Sono stato cum lo Camerlengo — {dash in the copy} lo quale intesa la casone de la mia venuta dice [blot] effecto essere necessario expectare la elecion d'un altro Papa, et per tractare la cossa cum la soa Sanctità, et che fra questo mezo posso andare da la Majestà del Re per strenzere la cossa cum si, et cussì farò, et de quello seguirà la S.V. ne serà avisata. Ha havuto el dicto Camerlengo molto grato et accepto quanto li ho dicto per vostra parte, et per le parole ha usato cum mi me pare essere molto volunteroso de havere et servare bona amicitia cum la S.V., et me ha commesso ve scriva che siati de bona voglia, perché qualuncha sia electo al papato voluntera farà de le cosse ve piaceranno. Dice etiandio ch'el serà amico el Segnore vostro padre, o almancho non li serà inimico, ma più crede che li serà amico e favorevele, et dio voglia che cussì sia. Se ha opinione che la elecione debia tocare o a Monsignore de Capua, o a Monsignore de Fermo, pur poteria essere che tocaria ad altri, perché me pare che sempre tochi a quello del quale comunamente non s'è facto pensiero. Se la Excellentia vostra facesse qualche vista et demostracione de volerse fare inance ne la Marcha, o altrove, siché qua ne venisse novelle, credo seria assay utile a rescaldare li animi de questi preti, et a farli più caldi al contribuire a la spesa vostra; et questo dico perché se [ha?] facto fondamento quasi certo che la S.V. ad ogni modo andarà a li favori et subsidii del {struck: del} a el prefato Signore vostro padre. La quale opinione però me sono sforzato de cavarli de la testa, et dicto che tale fondamento è vano, et che bene siati ben disposito bisogna che questa bona disposizione sia aiutata altramente che cum parole, cioè cum dinari. Ma per levargela ancora [gap?] {line ends with a flourish} Ex Roma vigesimo septimo Februarij. Vestre Excelencie Servulus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 55r-v, 57r = decipherment of f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) [canvases 53 right, 54 left, 55 right] Illustris ac excellens domine honorandissime. Sono stato da la Majestà del Re, et cum quelle rasone me sono acadute a la mente lo confortata et pregata a nome del mio Signore a prendere tanto majore cura et caricho de contribuire a la spesa vostra, quanto el bisogno è majore per la morte del Papa, dal quale non è più da expectare subventione alcuna. In effecto la soa Serenità è restata contenta non solamente de pagare quelo devia pagare el Papa, ma etiandio de contribuire de majore quantità non era stato rasonato da prima, cioè de ducati novantaquatro milia d'oro et in oro ogni anno et per dui anni come ha scripto el prefato Signore che'l restava contento de dui anni, et vole pagare li dicti dinari in questo modo, cioè vintimilia ducati nel mese presente, et altri xx m nel mese d'Aprile sequente al più tardi, et lo resto per la mità al fine de li sei mesi dal dì de la ferma vostra, et l'altra mità al fine del ano, et questo per lo primo anno: ma per respecto al secondo anno resta contento per tuto Martio del dicto anno de pagare quarantamilia ducati, et li altri LIIII m de sei mesi in sei mesi come è dicto de sopra, et cussì ha promesso la soa Serenità per capituli firmati et conclusi cum si et sigilati del suo sigillo, et ancora sotoscriti de soa propria mano: et debbe fare exbursare li dicti dinari a li tempi a qualuncha messo del prefato Signore, o vostro havendo expediente mandato a ciò. Per parte del Signore li è promesso, che non fareti contrasini contra li suoi, immo che bisognando mandarà el prefato Signore in suo aiuto, o tanti de li vostri, o de le altre gente ducale quante monta la spesa quale el fa per la conducta vostra, et ancora li è promesso, che quello pagherà el Papa serà electo debia pervenire in la soa Majestà. Per tanto de tuto aviso la Excelentia vostra acciò sapia quello è facto, et a bona fede doe cosse recordo. La prima che, o la Excelentia del Signore, o vui provediati de uno, quale habia mandato expediente a recevere el dinaro, et a confessare de haverlo recevuto, et ancora possa solicitarlo presso la Majestà del Re, perché sapeti bene, che dove va el dinaro non se po usare troppo diligentia. La secunda, che'l me pare necessario chiarire la prefata Majestà quanto più presto se po, come la conclusione è facta cum lui, aciò non se possa excusare, che per non essere chiarita non habia facta provisione al dinaro. Io li ho ben dato bona speranza de la conclusione secundo quello me dixe V.S., ma questo non credo che basti, et da mi non procederia a farli altra chiarezza, non havendo altro, o dal Signore, o da V.S., la quale me poterà scrivere la intentione soa circha de ciò {ciò written above a blotted word}, et io senza expectare altro la exequirò. Aviso ancora la excelentia vostra, che la Majestà del Re intende che in la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati, quali debe pagare, se includano li xx m del [gap; the copyist drew the cipher sign ꝺ+÷ in the margin]: Ma lui prende el caricho de fare che li pagli, e presto. Et per questo subito mandarà uno de li suoy, et pagandoli non se computavano in la quantità de li dicti xl m ducati se debeno pagare in Marcio et Aprile, ma in li altri se debeno pagare de sei mesi in sei mesi, et quando etiandio el [gap; ꝺ+÷ in the margin] non ne pagasse alcuna parte, resta però obligata la Majestà del Re a pagare la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati ogni anno. Se havesse possuto fare meglio, al che me sono sforzato quanto m'è stato possibile, lo haveria facto voluntera, ma non possendo ho acceptato quello ho possuto obtenere. Quanto a la elecione del Papa ve ho scripto per altre quello haveva inteso, adesso non me occorre altro, excepto che tutto se farà per haverne uno che sia amico, et non volendo esserlo se haverano de li modi da farlo pentire. Me recomando a V.S. et etiandio a la illustre Madona Bianca. Ex Roma tertio Marcij. Servitor devotus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 61r = decipherment of f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) [canvas 58 right] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Respondendo brevemente a quello me scrive la Excellentia Vostra per letre date a vintasete dal passato, dico che'l correro ducale, quale havite fato accompagnare, non me ha portato altra letra cha la vostra; sento bene che ne ha portate de le altre al Vescovo de Novara et a Misere Petro de Monferrato, et anchora a Simone Henrigono famiglo dal Signore vostro Padre, quale za molti meyse per la Signoria {"per la Signoria" underlined, "-ria" above} soa fa dimora in questo lito. Dico etiamdio che per tre meie {blot in the margin} ho avisato V.S. ____ de la morte dal Papa ____ {two underlined blanks} et de quanto me acadeva circha de ciò, ni da poy s'è innovato altro, excepto che li Cardinali questa sira sono intrati in conclave, et sperasse che assay tosto elezerano un altro Papa, et molto sono le opinione diverse a chi debia tocare la ellectione: Dio vegla che bona sia. Simelmente ho avisato per altre letre de la conclusione facta cum la Majestà dal Re. Et cussì le prime, como le segonde letre ho mandate a le mane de la Magnifica Madona Aura secondo me disse V.S., et per messi certi, e debeno le dicte letre esser zonte a salvamento. Da mo innance drizarò simile letre a Misser Angelo in Urbino como scriviti. Et continuamente avisarò V.S. de le cosse come passarano. Adesso ve mando alligate a le presenti certe letre de la Majestà dal Re, per le quale intenderite la bona dispositione soa, avisando V.S. che la intesso molto voluntera quello li ho dicto per vostra parte, et maxime ha gustato quello dicesti de havere alienato l'animo da le cosse del reame, et demonstrato una bona voluntà de volerve havere per tuto suo. Me recommando a la S.V. Ex Roma die quarto Martii 1447. per V.S. servitorem devotum Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 68 = decipherment of f. 69 (Rome, 6 Mar 1447) [canvas 65, upper leaf] Illustris ac excellens domine honorandissime. In questa hora decima septima, o circha, è publicato Papa Monsignore da Cologna {so in the copy: Tommaso Parentucelli, elected as Nicholas V on 6 March 1447, was cardinal-bishop of Bologna; the cipher was not checked at this word}. Credo firmamente che serà amico, e presto me sforzarò de vederne la experientia circa le cosse me sono comesse. Et de quello seguirà V.S. ne serà avisata, la quale me po avisare, se gli pare che sia da servare per mi più uno modo che un altro. Me ricommando a la Excelencia vostra. Ex Roma sexto Marcij 1447. Per Servitorem V.V. Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francischo Sfortie etc. ## f. 74r-v = decipherment of f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) [canvases 71 right, 72 left] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Da poi ve scripsi la ellectione del novo Papa sono stato quello dì de la ellectione per non perdere tempo a li pedi de la soa Beatitudine, et da poy alchune parole generale dicte reallegrandome a nome del Duca de la ellectione soa toccai etiandio el facto del dinaro per V.S.; in effecto me pare che la Sanctità soa insieme cum li Cardinali habia presso deliberatione de procurare pace in Italia, et de mandare per questa caxone el Camerlengo et lo Vicecanciellero insieme da la Majestà del Re, quale sono partiti questo dì, ma no li reusirano li pensieri, perché lo Re, dal quale sono stato per questa casone un'altra volta, delibera de darli molto bene ad intendere, et specialmente al Camerlengo, perché l'altro è Veneciano, che queste parole de pace non gli piaceno, excepto se non fano prima la provisione del dinaro per V.S., et de le gente per mandare insieme cum la soa Majestà, a ciò che cum questa via sia proveduto a la securezza del stato del prefato Duca, et li inimici temendo le provisione se reducano a meglore condictione de pace, o non volendola per amore se gli possa redure cum la forcia. Delibera etiandio la soa Majestà, se questo parlare non moverà el Papa et li Cardinali a fare altra deliberatione meglore et più grata de aprirli come essa Majestà intende tore in si el carrego de pagare la spesa vostra, et dire che siano certi ge la farà pagare tuta a loro, et se anchora questo non aiutarà, mostra de volere usare altro che parole, cioè venire a li facti dicendo, che li preti sono homini da bastonate, non da pregare. Non so quello seguirà, pur non sono anchora sanza speranza, che'l Papa et li Cardinali intendando el malcontentamento del Re se debiano movere a piglare meglore deliberatione; de quello seguirà V.S. ne sarà avisata; et forse como per altre ho scripto non serà altro, che bene che V.S. facia de le demonstratione per timorezare anchora più la brigata et redurla a quello desideramo. Ho recordato anchora a la Majestà del Re el facto de li dinari per V.S., et me ha resposto che sanza fallo li meterà tale ordine non vi mancharano a li termini, et simelmente ha dicto che in questa septimana aviarà el suo, quale el manda dal Signore [gap; the copyist drew ꝺ+÷ in the margin] per quelli vinti millia ducati. Me ricommando a la Excellentia Vostra, et maraviglo che da si non habia mai havuto ni letra ni risposta. Ex Roma die octavo Marcij 1447. per Servitorem devotum Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. Translation decipherments_18c_en.md # English translation of the clear copies of Barbavara's cipher letters (BnF italien 1584) Translated 28 Oct 2026 by Claude Opus 5.5 from `decipherments_18c.md`. Now I have warned him as much as is needed, and he will call at the house of Cecco, your chancellor, as you write. I send by him the safe-conduct requested for those two men of yours, and next Wednesday I shall go to [Atachio?] by way of San Giovanni in Marignano, according to your command, and I shall keep all the ways they give me for finding myself with Your Lordship. With Lord Sigismondo I have kept the manner Your Excellency advises me of; to whom I commend myself. Rimini, 13 February. Your Lordship's servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 48r-v = f. 49 (Rome, 27 Feb 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Having arrived here I found the Pope had passed from this life, as you will have heard, and he has indeed wished to do as Your Lordship used to say: to die so as to do harm not only living but also dying. I have been with the Camerlengo, who, having heard the reason for my coming, says that in effect it is necessary to wait for the election of another Pope and to treat the matter with His Holiness, and that meanwhile I can go to His Majesty the King to tighten the matter with him; and so I shall do, and Your Lordship will be told what follows. The said Camerlengo received very gratefully all I told him on your behalf, and from the words he used with me he seems to me very willing to have and keep good friendship with Your Lordship. He charged me to write to you to be of good heart, because whoever is elected to the papacy will gladly do things that please you. He says too that he will be a friend of the lord your father, or at least not his enemy, but rather believes he will be his friend and favourable, and God grant it be so. It is thought that the election must fall either to Monsignor of Capua or to Monsignor of Fermo; yet it could be that it falls to others, because it seems to me it always falls to the one no one has commonly thought of. If Your Excellency made some show and demonstration of wanting to advance into the Marche or elsewhere, so that news of it came here, I believe it would be very useful to warm the minds of these priests and make them hotter to contribute to your expenses; and I say this because they have built an almost certain foundation that Your Lordship will in any case go to the favour and help of the said lord your father. That opinion, however, I have striven to get out of their heads, and said that such a foundation is vain, and that, though you are well disposed, this good disposition must be helped otherwise than with words, that is with money. But to take it from them still [gap?]. Rome, 27 February. Your Excellency's little servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## ff. 55r-v, 57r = f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. I have been to His Majesty the King, and with such reasons as came to mind I urged and begged him, in the name of my lord, to take all the greater care and burden of contributing to your expenses as the need is greater through the death of the Pope, from whom no subsidy is to be expected any more. In effect His Serenity has been content not only to pay what the Pope was to pay, but also to contribute a greater sum than had first been discussed, namely ninety-four thousand ducats of gold, in gold, every year and for two years, as the said lord wrote that he was content with two years. He will pay the said money in this way: twenty thousand ducats this month, and another twenty thousand in the coming month of April at the latest, and the rest half at the end of six months from the day of your engagement and the other half at the end of the year, and this for the first year; but for the second year he is content to pay forty thousand ducats by the whole of March of that year, and the other 54 thousand from six months to six months as said above. And so His Serenity has promised, by articles signed and concluded with him, sealed with his seal and also signed in his own hand; and he is to have the said money paid out at the due times to whatever messenger of the said lord, or of yours, holds a sufficient mandate for it. On the lord's part he has been promised that you will make no attacks on his men; rather, if need be, the said lord will send to his aid either as many of your men, or of the other ducal troops, as amounts to the expense he bears for your condotta; and he has also been promised that what the Pope pays, once he is elected, shall come to His Majesty. Of all this I inform Your Excellency so that you know what has been done, and in good faith I recall two things. The first: that either His Excellency the lord or you provide someone with a sufficient mandate to receive the money and to acknowledge receiving it, and also to press for it with His Majesty the King, because you know well that where money is concerned one cannot use too much diligence. The second: it seems to me necessary to make clear to His Majesty as soon as possible that the conclusion has been made with him, so that he cannot excuse himself that, not having been made certain, he has not provided the money. I have indeed given him good hope of the conclusion according to what Your Lordship told me, but I do not think that is enough, and from my side I would not go on to give him any other assurance, having nothing else either from the lord or from Your Lordship, who may write to me your intention about this, and I shall carry it out without waiting for anything else. I inform Your Excellency also that His Majesty the King understands that in the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats which he is to pay are included the 20 thousand of the [gap: the lord of Ferrara?]; but he takes on himself the burden of making him pay them, and soon. For this he will at once send one of his men, and when they are paid they will not be counted in the said 40 thousand ducats to be paid in March and April, but in the others to be paid from six months to six months; and even if the [gap: lord of Ferrara?] paid no part of them, His Majesty the King remains bound to pay the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats every year. Had I been able to do better, which I strove for as far as was possible, I would gladly have done it; but not being able, I accepted what I could obtain. As for the election of the Pope, I wrote to you in other letters what I had heard; now I have nothing else to add, except that everything will be done to have one who is a friend, and if he will not be, they will have ways to make him repent. I commend myself to Your Lordship and also to the illustrious Madonna Bianca. Rome, 3 March. Devoted servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 61r = f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Replying briefly to what Your Excellency writes to me in letters of the twenty-seventh of last month, I say that the ducal courier whom you had escorted brought me no letter but yours; I hear indeed that he brought others to the Bishop of Novara and to Messer Pietro of Monferrato, and also to Simone Arrigoni, servant of the lord your father, who has stayed in this place many months for His Lordship. I say also that by three letters of mine I have informed Your Lordship of the death of the Pope and of what happened to me about it; nor has anything new happened since, except that the cardinals entered the conclave this evening, and it is hoped they will very soon elect another Pope, and opinions are very divided as to whom the election should fall to: God grant it be a good one. Likewise I informed you by other letters of the conclusion made with His Majesty the King. Both the first and the second letters I sent into the hands of the Magnificent Madonna Aura, as Your Lordship told me, and by sure messengers, and the said letters should have arrived safely. From now on I shall direct such letters to Messer Angelo in Urbino, as you write. And I shall continually inform Your Lordship of things as they happen. Now I send you, enclosed with these, certain letters of His Majesty the King, by which you will understand his good disposition; informing Your Lordship that he heard very gladly what I told him on your behalf, and above all he relished what you said of having turned your mind from the affairs of the Kingdom, and showed a good will to have you wholly his. I commend myself to Your Lordship. Rome, 4 March 1447, by Your Lordship's devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 68 = f. 69 (Rome, 6 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. At this seventeenth hour or about, Monsignor of "Cologna" [so the copy; Tommaso Parentucelli, cardinal of Bologna] has been proclaimed Pope. I firmly believe he will be a friend, and I shall soon strive to see proof of it in the matters entrusted to me. Of what follows Your Lordship will be informed; and you may tell me whether it seems to you that one way rather than another should be kept by me. I commend myself to Your Excellency. Rome, 6 March 1447, by Your Lordship's servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 74r-v = f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Since I wrote to you of the election of the new Pope, I was, on the very day of the election, so as to lose no time, at the feet of His Holiness, and after some general words rejoicing in the name of the Duke at his election I touched also on the matter of money for Your Lordship. In effect it seems to me that His Holiness together with the cardinals has resolved to procure peace in Italy, and for this reason to send the Camerlengo and the Vice-Chancellor together to His Majesty the King; they left today, but their plans will not succeed, because the King, whom I have seen again for this reason, means to make them understand very well, and especially the Camerlengo (because the other is a Venetian), that these words of peace do not please him unless they first make provision of money for Your Lordship, and of troops to send together with His Majesty, so that by this way the security of the state of the said Duke is provided for, and the enemies, fearing the provisions, are brought to better terms of peace, or, not wanting it out of love, can be brought to it by force. His Majesty resolves also, if this speech does not move the Pope and the cardinals to some better and more agreeable resolution, to declare to them that His Majesty means to take on himself the burden of paying your expenses, and to tell them to be sure he will make them pay it all, and if even this does not help, he shows he will use other than words, that is, come to deeds, saying that priests are men to be beaten, not begged. I do not know what will follow; still I am not yet without hope that the Pope and the cardinals, understanding the King's discontent, may be moved to take a better resolution; of what follows Your Lordship will be informed. And perhaps, as I have written elsewhere, nothing else will do but that Your Lordship make some demonstrations, to frighten the company still more and bring it to what we desire. I reminded His Majesty the King again of the matter of the money for Your Lordship, and he answered that without fail he will give such orders that it will not fail you at the terms, and likewise he said that this week he will send his man, whom he is sending to the lord [gap: of Ferrara?] for those twenty thousand ducats. I commend myself to Your Excellency, and I marvel that I have never had from you either letter or answer. Rome, 8 March 1447, by your devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. Marcolino Barbavara, Rome, 4 Mar 1447 (cipher f. 62; copy f. 61r) The cardinals have entered the conclave; letters go by Madonna Aura and Messer Angelo in Urbino; Alfonso's letters enclosed, the King pleased that Sforza has turned from the Kingdom. Essendo zonto qua ho trovato el Papa essere passato de questa vita come haveriti inteso, et ha pur voluto fare come diceva la S.V., cioè morire per fare male non solamente vivendo, ma etiandio morendo. Sono stato cum lo Camerlengo — {dash in the copy} lo quale intesa la casone de la mia venuta dice [blot] effecto essere necessario expectare la elecion d'un altro Papa, et per tractare la cossa cum la soa Sanctità, et che fra questo mezo posso andare da la Majestà del Re per strenzere la cossa cum si, et cussì farò, et de quello seguirà la S.V. ne serà avisata. Ha havuto el dicto Camerlengo molto grato et accepto quanto li ho dicto per vostra parte, et per le parole ha usato cum mi me pare essere molto volunteroso de havere et servare bona amicitia cum la S.V., et me ha commesso ve scriva che siati de bona voglia, perché qualuncha sia electo al papato voluntera farà de le cosse ve piaceranno. Dice etiandio ch'el serà amico el Segnore vostro padre, o almancho non li serà inimico, ma più crede che li serà amico e favorevele, et dio voglia che cussì sia. Ma per levargela ancora [gap?] {line ends with a flourish} Ex Roma vigesimo septimo Februarij. Vestre Excelencie Servulus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 55r-v, 57r = decipherment of f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) [canvases 53 right, 54 left, 55 right] Illustris ac excellens domine honorandissime. Sono stato da la Majestà del Re, et cum quelle rasone me sono acadute a la mente lo confortata et pregata a nome del mio Signore a prendere tanto majore cura et caricho de contribuire a la spesa vostra, quanto el bisogno è majore per la morte del Papa, dal quale non è più da expectare subventione alcuna. In effecto la soa Serenità è restata contenta non solamente de pagare quelo devia pagare el Papa, ma etiandio de contribuire de majore quantità non era stato rasonato da prima, cioè de ducati novantaquatro milia d'oro et in oro ogni anno et per dui anni come ha scripto el prefato Signore che'l restava contento de dui anni, et vole pagare li dicti dinari in questo modo, cioè vintimilia ducati nel mese presente, et altri xx m nel mese d'Aprile sequente al più tardi, et lo resto per la mità al fine de li sei mesi dal dì de la ferma vostra, et l'altra mità al fine del ano, et questo per lo primo anno: ma per respecto al secondo anno resta contento per tuto Martio del dicto anno de pagare quarantamilia ducati, et li altri LIIII m de sei mesi in sei mesi come è dicto de sopra, et cussì ha promesso la soa Serenità per capituli firmati et conclusi cum si et sigilati del suo sigillo, et ancora sotoscriti de soa propria mano: et debbe fare exbursare li dicti dinari a li tempi a qualuncha messo del prefato Signore, o vostro havendo expediente mandato a ciò. Per parte del Signore li è promesso, che non fareti contrasini contra li suoi, immo che bisognando mandarà el prefato Signore in suo aiuto, o tanti de li vostri, o de le altre gente ducale quante monta la spesa quale el fa per la conducta vostra, et ancora li è promesso, che quello pagherà el Papa serà electo debia pervenire in la soa Majestà. Per tanto de tuto aviso la Excelentia vostra acciò sapia quello è facto, et a bona fede doe cosse recordo. La prima che, o la Excelentia del Signore, o vui provediati de uno, quale habia mandato expediente a recevere el dinaro, et a confessare de haverlo recevuto, et ancora possa solicitarlo presso la Majestà del Re, perché sapeti bene, che dove va el dinaro non se po usare troppo diligentia. La secunda, che'l me pare necessario chiarire la prefata Majestà quanto più presto se po, come la conclusione è facta cum lui, aciò non se possa excusare, che per non essere chiarita non habia facta provisione al dinaro. Io li ho ben dato bona speranza de la conclusione secundo quello me dixe V.S., ma questo non credo che basti, et da mi non procederia a farli altra chiarezza, non havendo altro, o dal Signore, o da V.S., la quale me poterà scrivere la intentione soa circha de ciò {ciò written above a blotted word}, et io senza expectare altro la exequirò. Aviso ancora la excelentia vostra, che la Majestà del Re intende che in la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati, quali debe pagare, se includano li xx m del [gap; the copyist drew the cipher sign ꝺ+÷ in the margin]: Ma lui prende el caricho de fare che li pagli, e presto. Et per questo subito mandarà uno de li suoy, et pagandoli non se computavano in la quantità de li dicti xl m ducati se debeno pagare in Marcio et Aprile, ma in li altri se debeno pagare de sei mesi in sei mesi, et quando etiandio el [gap; ꝺ+÷ in the margin] non ne pagasse alcuna parte, resta però obligata la Majestà del Re a pagare la dicta summa de novantaquatro milia ducati ogni anno. Se havesse possuto fare meglio, al che me sono sforzato quanto m'è stato possibile, lo haveria facto voluntera, ma non possendo ho acceptato quello ho possuto obtenere. Quanto a la elecione del Papa ve ho scripto per altre quello haveva inteso, adesso non me occorre altro, excepto che tutto se farà per haverne uno che sia amico, et non volendo esserlo se haverano de li modi da farlo pentire. Me recomando a V.S. et etiandio a la illustre Madona Bianca. Ex Roma tertio Marcij. Servitor devotus Marcolinus. {Address:} Illustri domino Francisco Sfortie etc. ## f. 61r = decipherment of f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) [canvas 58 right] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Dico etiamdio che per tre meie {blot in the margin} ho avisato V.S. ____ de la morte dal Papa ____ {two underlined blanks} et de quanto me acadeva circha de ciò, ni da poy s'è innovato altro, excepto che li Cardinali questa sira sono intrati in conclave, et sperasse che assay tosto elezerano un altro Papa, et molto sono le opinione diverse a chi debia tocare la ellectione: Dio vegla che bona sia. Simelmente ho avisato per altre letre de la conclusione facta cum la Majestà dal Re. Et cussì le prime, como le segonde letre ho mandate a le mane de la Magnifica Madona Aura secondo me disse V.S., et per messi certi, e debeno le dicte letre esser zonte a salvamento. Adesso ve mando alligate a le presenti certe letre de la Majestà dal Re, per le quale intenderite la bona dispositione soa, avisando V.S. che la intesso molto voluntera quello li ho dicto per vostra parte, et maxime ha gustato quello dicesti de havere alienato l'animo da le cosse del reame, et demonstrato una bona voluntà de volerve havere per tuto suo. Me recommando a la S.V. In questa hora decima septima, o circha, è publicato Papa Monsignore da Cologna {so in the copy: Tommaso Parentucelli, elected as Nicholas V on 6 March 1447, was cardinal-bishop of Bologna; the cipher was not checked at this word}. Credo firmamente che serà amico, e presto me sforzarò de vederne la experientia circa le cosse me sono comesse. Et de quello seguirà V.S. ne serà avisata, la quale me po avisare, se gli pare che sia da servare per mi più uno modo che un altro. Me ricommando a la Excelencia vostra. Ex Roma sexto Marcij 1447. Per Servitorem V.V. Marcolinum de Barbavariis. {Address:} Illustri domino Francischo Sfortie etc. ## f. 74r-v = decipherment of f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) [canvases 71 right, 72 left] Illustris ac excelse domine honorandissime. Da poi ve scripsi la ellectione del novo Papa sono stato quello dì de la ellectione per non perdere tempo a li pedi de la soa Beatitudine, et da poy alchune parole generale dicte reallegrandome a nome del Duca de la ellectione soa toccai etiandio el facto del dinaro per V.S.; in effecto me pare che la Sanctità soa insieme cum li Cardinali habia presso deliberatione de procurare pace in Italia, et de mandare per questa caxone el Camerlengo et lo Vicecanciellero insieme da la Majestà del Re, quale sono partiti questo dì, ma no li reusirano li pensieri, perché lo Re, dal quale sono stato per questa casone un'altra volta, delibera de darli molto bene ad intendere, et specialmente al Camerlengo, perché l'altro è Veneciano, che queste parole de pace non gli piaceno, excepto se non fano prima la provisione del dinaro per V.S., et de le gente per mandare insieme cum la soa Majestà, a ciò che cum questa via sia proveduto a la securezza del stato del prefato Duca, et li inimici temendo le provisione se reducano a meglore condictione de pace, o non volendola per amore se gli possa redure cum la forcia. Delibera etiandio la soa Majestà, se questo parlare non moverà el Papa et li Cardinali a fare altra deliberatione meglore et più grata de aprirli come essa Majestà intende tore in si el carrego de pagare la spesa vostra, et dire che siano certi ge la farà pagare tuta a loro, et se anchora questo non aiutarà, mostra de volere usare altro che parole, cioè venire a li facti dicendo, che li preti sono homini da bastonate, non da pregare. Non so quello seguirà, pur non sono anchora sanza speranza, che'l Papa et li Cardinali intendando el malcontentamento del Re se debiano movere a piglare meglore deliberatione; de quello seguirà V.S. ne sarà avisata; et forse como per altre ho scripto non serà altro, che bene che V.S. facia de le demonstratione per timorezare anchora più la brigata et redurla a quello desideramo. Ho recordato anchora a la Majestà del Re el facto de li dinari per V.S., et me ha resposto che sanza fallo li meterà tale ordine non vi mancharano a li termini, et simelmente ha dicto che in questa septimana aviarà el suo, quale el manda dal Signore [gap; the copyist drew ꝺ+÷ in the margin] per quelli vinti millia ducati. Me ricommando a la Excellentia Vostra, et maraviglo che da si non habia mai havuto ni letra ni risposta. [gap] = a blank left by the copyist; [?] = uncertain. ## f. 39 = f. 40 (Rimini, 13 Feb 1447) If the courier has not kept the ways Your Lordship would have wished, it came about because, those of the [gap] being his, it did not seem to him that he needed to come with any other caution. Now I have warned him as much as is needed, and he will call at the house of Cecco, your chancellor, as you write. I send by him the safe-conduct requested for those two men of yours, and next Wednesday I shall go to [Atachio?] by way of San Giovanni in Marignano, according to your command, and I shall keep all the ways they give me for finding myself with Your Lordship. With Lord Sigismondo I have kept the manner Your Excellency advises me of; to whom I commend myself. Rimini, 13 February. Your Lordship's servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 48r-v = f. 49 (Rome, 27 Feb 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Having arrived here I found the Pope had passed from this life, as you will have heard, and he has indeed wished to do as Your Lordship used to say: to die so as to do harm not only living but also dying. I have been with the Camerlengo, who, having heard the reason for my coming, says that in effect it is necessary to wait for the election of another Pope and to treat the matter with His Holiness, and that meanwhile I can go to His Majesty the King to tighten the matter with him; and so I shall do, and Your Lordship will be told what follows. The said Camerlengo received very gratefully all I told him on your behalf, and from the words he used with me he seems to me very willing to have and keep good friendship with Your Lordship. He charged me to write to you to be of good heart, because whoever is elected to the papacy will gladly do things that please you. He says too that he will be a friend of the lord your father, or at least not his enemy, but rather believes he will be his friend and favourable, and God grant it be so. It is thought that the election must fall either to Monsignor of Capua or to Monsignor of Fermo; yet it could be that it falls to others, because it seems to me it always falls to the one no one has commonly thought of. If Your Excellency made some show and demonstration of wanting to advance into the Marche or elsewhere, so that news of it came here, I believe it would be very useful to warm the minds of these priests and make them hotter to contribute to your expenses; and I say this because they have built an almost certain foundation that Your Lordship will in any case go to the favour and help of the said lord your father. That opinion, however, I have striven to get out of their heads, and said that such a foundation is vain, and that, though you are well disposed, this good disposition must be helped otherwise than with words, that is with money. But to take it from them still [gap?]. Rome, 27 February. Your Excellency's little servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## ff. 55r-v, 57r = f. 56 (Rome, 3 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. I have been to His Majesty the King, and with such reasons as came to mind I urged and begged him, in the name of my lord, to take all the greater care and burden of contributing to your expenses as the need is greater through the death of the Pope, from whom no subsidy is to be expected any more. In effect His Serenity has been content not only to pay what the Pope was to pay, but also to contribute a greater sum than had first been discussed, namely ninety-four thousand ducats of gold, in gold, every year and for two years, as the said lord wrote that he was content with two years. He will pay the said money in this way: twenty thousand ducats this month, and another twenty thousand in the coming month of April at the latest, and the rest half at the end of six months from the day of your engagement and the other half at the end of the year, and this for the first year; but for the second year he is content to pay forty thousand ducats by the whole of March of that year, and the other 54 thousand from six months to six months as said above. And so His Serenity has promised, by articles signed and concluded with him, sealed with his seal and also signed in his own hand; and he is to have the said money paid out at the due times to whatever messenger of the said lord, or of yours, holds a sufficient mandate for it. On the lord's part he has been promised that you will make no attacks on his men; rather, if need be, the said lord will send to his aid either as many of your men, or of the other ducal troops, as amounts to the expense he bears for your condotta; and he has also been promised that what the Pope pays, once he is elected, shall come to His Majesty. Of all this I inform Your Excellency so that you know what has been done, and in good faith I recall two things. The first: that either His Excellency the lord or you provide someone with a sufficient mandate to receive the money and to acknowledge receiving it, and also to press for it with His Majesty the King, because you know well that where money is concerned one cannot use too much diligence. The second: it seems to me necessary to make clear to His Majesty as soon as possible that the conclusion has been made with him, so that he cannot excuse himself that, not having been made certain, he has not provided the money. I have indeed given him good hope of the conclusion according to what Your Lordship told me, but I do not think that is enough, and from my side I would not go on to give him any other assurance, having nothing else either from the lord or from Your Lordship, who may write to me your intention about this, and I shall carry it out without waiting for anything else. I inform Your Excellency also that His Majesty the King understands that in the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats which he is to pay are included the 20 thousand of the [gap: the lord of Ferrara?]; but he takes on himself the burden of making him pay them, and soon. For this he will at once send one of his men, and when they are paid they will not be counted in the said 40 thousand ducats to be paid in March and April, but in the others to be paid from six months to six months; and even if the [gap: lord of Ferrara?] paid no part of them, His Majesty the King remains bound to pay the said sum of ninety-four thousand ducats every year. Had I been able to do better, which I strove for as far as was possible, I would gladly have done it; but not being able, I accepted what I could obtain. As for the election of the Pope, I wrote to you in other letters what I had heard; now I have nothing else to add, except that everything will be done to have one who is a friend, and if he will not be, they will have ways to make him repent. I commend myself to Your Lordship and also to the illustrious Madonna Bianca. Rome, 3 March. Devoted servant, Marcolino. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 61r = f. 62 (Rome, 4 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Replying briefly to what Your Excellency writes to me in letters of the twenty-seventh of last month, I say that the ducal courier whom you had escorted brought me no letter but yours; I hear indeed that he brought others to the Bishop of Novara and to Messer Pietro of Monferrato, and also to Simone Arrigoni, servant of the lord your father, who has stayed in this place many months for His Lordship. I say also that by three letters of mine I have informed Your Lordship of the death of the Pope and of what happened to me about it; nor has anything new happened since, except that the cardinals entered the conclave this evening, and it is hoped they will very soon elect another Pope, and opinions are very divided as to whom the election should fall to: God grant it be a good one. Likewise I informed you by other letters of the conclusion made with His Majesty the King. Both the first and the second letters I sent into the hands of the Magnificent Madonna Aura, as Your Lordship told me, and by sure messengers, and the said letters should have arrived safely. From now on I shall direct such letters to Messer Angelo in Urbino, as you write. And I shall continually inform Your Lordship of things as they happen. Now I send you, enclosed with these, certain letters of His Majesty the King, by which you will understand his good disposition; informing Your Lordship that he heard very gladly what I told him on your behalf, and above all he relished what you said of having turned your mind from the affairs of the Kingdom, and showed a good will to have you wholly his. I commend myself to Your Lordship. Rome, 4 March 1447, by Your Lordship's devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 68 = f. 69 (Rome, 6 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. At this seventeenth hour or about, Monsignor of "Cologna" [so the copy; Tommaso Parentucelli, cardinal of Bologna] has been proclaimed Pope. I firmly believe he will be a friend, and I shall soon strive to see proof of it in the matters entrusted to me. Of what follows Your Lordship will be informed; and you may tell me whether it seems to you that one way rather than another should be kept by me. I commend myself to Your Excellency. Rome, 6 March 1447, by Your Lordship's servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. ## f. 74r-v = f. 75 (Rome, 8 Mar 1447) Illustrious and excellent, most honoured lord. Since I wrote to you of the election of the new Pope, I was, on the very day of the election, so as to lose no time, at the feet of His Holiness, and after some general words rejoicing in the name of the Duke at his election I touched also on the matter of money for Your Lordship. In effect it seems to me that His Holiness together with the cardinals has resolved to procure peace in Italy, and for this reason to send the Camerlengo and the Vice-Chancellor together to His Majesty the King; they left today, but their plans will not succeed, because the King, whom I have seen again for this reason, means to make them understand very well, and especially the Camerlengo (because the other is a Venetian), that these words of peace do not please him unless they first make provision of money for Your Lordship, and of troops to send together with His Majesty, so that by this way the security of the state of the said Duke is provided for, and the enemies, fearing the provisions, are brought to better terms of peace, or, not wanting it out of love, can be brought to it by force. His Majesty resolves also, if this speech does not move the Pope and the cardinals to some better and more agreeable resolution, to declare to them that His Majesty means to take on himself the burden of paying your expenses, and to tell them to be sure he will make them pay it all, and if even this does not help, he shows he will use other than words, that is, come to deeds, saying that priests are men to be beaten, not begged. I do not know what will follow; still I am not yet without hope that the Pope and the cardinals, understanding the King's discontent, may be moved to take a better resolution; of what follows Your Lordship will be informed. And perhaps, as I have written elsewhere, nothing else will do but that Your Lordship make some demonstrations, to frighten the company still more and bring it to what we desire. I reminded His Majesty the King again of the matter of the money for Your Lordship, and he answered that without fail he will give such orders that it will not fail you at the terms, and likewise he said that this week he will send his man, whom he is sending to the lord [gap: of Ferrara?] for those twenty thousand ducats. I commend myself to Your Excellency, and I marvel that I have never had from you either letter or answer. Rome, 8 March 1447, by your devoted servant Marcolino de Barbavara. To the illustrious lord Francesco Sforza. Marcolino Barbavara, Rome, 6 Mar 1447 (cipher f. 69; copy f. 68) The new pope is proclaimed at about the seventeenth hour: Tommaso Parentucelli, Nicholas V ("Monsignore da Cologna" in the copy, for Bologna). Transcription: none of the cipher. The cipher leaf was not transcribed sign by sign: the late clear copy filed with it is a complete text (spot checks with the R1857 key agree). Essendo zonto qua ho trovato el Papa essere passato de questa vita come haveriti inteso, et ha pur voluto fare come diceva la S.V., cioè morire per fare male non solamente vivendo, ma etiandio morendo.
